decision_reason: The most critical result — the CDC FluView Week 40 ending October 5, 2024 report (https://www.cdc.gov/fluview/surveillance/2024-week-40.html) — was identified in the result set and its snippet contains directly task-relevant evidence (influenza A subtype breakdown, H5 cases in California, percent positivity stability). However, two planned queries from iteration 1 (it1_q3: WHO/PAHO validation; it1_q4: news search) were NOT executed. Source diversity is critically limited: all 16 results came exclusively from cdc.gov, with no WHO/PAHO, no news, and no state-level health department sources. The target fields include subnational_location, locality, deaths, hospitalizations, and cases_confirmed — fields that may be partially covered by the CDC report but benefit from independent corroboration and subnational detail. A second iteration is warranted to: (1) execute the WHO/PAHO validation query, (2) execute a news search for the specific week, (3) target the CDC FluSurv-NET hospitalization data specifically for week 40 2024, and (4) attempt a state-level or MMWR early release query for subnational data. This is the final permitted iteration (max_iterations=2), so all four query slots must be used efficiently.
coverage_assessment: Partial. The CDC FluView 2024-week-40 report URL was surfaced and its snippet confirms task-period relevance (week ending October 5, 2024). However, the snippet alone does not provide complete quantitative data for all target fields (deaths, hospitalizations, confirmed case counts, subnational breakdown). The remaining 14 accepted results are from wrong time periods (2025–2026 season) and are not task-relevant. No WHO/PAHO, news, or state-level sources were retrieved. Two of four planned iteration-1 queries were not executed.
source_diversity_assessment: Very low. 100% of results (16/16) came from cdc.gov. No international organization reports (WHO, PAHO), no news sources, no state health department pages, and no MMWR publications were retrieved. The task requires source_url and source_type diversity for robust evidence collection. A second iteration targeting non-CDC channels is necessary.
trustworthiness_assessment: The one task-relevant result (CDC FluView 2024-week-40) is highly trustworthy — cdc.gov is the gold-standard U.S. influenza surveillance authority. The snippet confirms the correct week (ending October 5, 2024) and contains verifiable surveillance signals. However, single-source reliance is insufficient for a complete evidence record; independent validation from WHO/PAHO or news sources citing official data is needed.
disease_location_time_fit_assessment: The CDC FluView 2024-week-40 result is an exact fit: disease=Influenza, location=United States (national + HHS regions), time=week ending October 5, 2024 (= MMWR week 40, covering Sep 29–Oct 5 2024). The snippet confirms influenza A subtype data and two H5 cases in California. All other 14 accepted results are from 2025–2026 and are out-of-scope for the task window.
corroboration_potential_assessment: Moderate-to-high. WHO global influenza updates and PAHO regional bulletins routinely cite U.S. CDC data for the corresponding MMWR week, providing independent corroboration. News sources (AP, Reuters, NPR, STAT News) frequently report on early flu season activity citing CDC figures. FluSurv-NET hospitalization data for week 40 2024 may be available as a separate CDC data product. MMWR early release notes may contain additional quantitative detail. All of these are reachable via targeted queries in iteration 2.

decision_reason: Both permitted iterations have been fully executed (max_iterations=2, max_queries_per_iteration=4, all 8 planned queries executed across iterations 1 and 2). The result set now contains a strong, multi-source evidence base for the task window (MMWR Week 40, Sep 29–Oct 5, 2024): (1) the definitive CDC FluView Week 40 ending October 5, 2024 report (cdc.gov/fluview/surveillance/2024-week-40.html) with national-level virological data, percent positivity, HHS-region breakdown, and H5 case note; (2) the Mississippi MSDH state-level ILI surveillance PDF explicitly dated Sept. 29–Oct. 5, 2024 (msdh.ms.gov), providing subnational_location and ILI rate data; (3) the PAHO Regional Update for Epidemiological Week 40 (published 11 October 2024, paho.org) covering the Americas including North America, providing independent international corroboration; (4) the ECDC Communicable Disease Threats Report for 28 September–4 October 2024 (ecdc.europa.eu), covering the exact task window with avian influenza A(H5N1) human case context; and (5) additional accepted candidates from cidrap.umn.edu, contagionlive.com, reuters.com, globalbiodefense.com, and infectioncontroltoday.com that may contain news-sourced evidence quotes. Source diversity is now adequate across official public health agencies (CDC, MSDH), international organizations (PAHO, ECDC), and news/specialist outlets. The iteration cap has been reached and no further queries are permitted under the stated bounds.
coverage_assessment: Coverage is good for the task window. National-level U.S. influenza surveillance data for MMWR Week 40 (Sep 29–Oct 5, 2024) is anchored by the CDC FluView report, which provides virological breakdown (56 influenza A viruses; 55.8% H1N1pdm09, 44.2% H3N2), percent positivity stability, ED visit trends, and a note on two H5 human cases in California. Subnational coverage is partially addressed by the Mississippi MSDH Week 40 PDF (ILI rate 2.8%, up from 2.3% prior week). PAHO Week 40 bulletin provides regional context for North America. ECDC CDTR covers the exact date range. News/specialist outlets (cidrap, contagionlive, reuters, etc.) are present in the accepted candidate pool and may yield additional evidence quotes. Gaps remain for: (a) explicit hospitalization counts (FluSurv-NET quantitative rates not confirmed in snippets); (b) confirmed deaths for the specific week; (c) subnational data beyond Mississippi. These gaps are consistent with the nature of early-season Week 40 data, where activity is at low/baseline levels and detailed hospitalization/mortality tables may not yet be populated.
source_diversity_assessment: Substantially improved from iteration 1 (CDC-only) to iteration 2. Domain diversity now spans: cdc.gov (6), paho.org (4), msdh.ms.gov (1), ecdc.europa.eu (1), who.int (1), cidrap.umn.edu (1), contagionlive.com (2), reuters.com (1), globalbiodefense.com (1), infectioncontroltoday.com (1), plus lower-value sources. Source type diversity covers: official public health agency (CDC, MSDH), international organization (PAHO, ECDC, WHO), news/specialist media (CIDRAP, Reuters, Contagion Live), and academic/literature (JMIR, PMC). This is adequate for a one-week surveillance window at the start of a low-activity flu season.
trustworthiness_assessment: High. The primary source (CDC FluView 2024-week-40.html) is from the gold-standard U.S. influenza surveillance system on the cdc.gov domain. The MSDH PDF is from an official state health department (msdh.ms.gov) with explicit Week 40 dating. PAHO (paho.org) is an authoritative WHO regional office. ECDC (ecdc.europa.eu) is an authoritative EU public health agency. News/specialist sources (cidrap.umn.edu, reuters.com, contagionlive.com) are credible secondary sources. Low-trust results (facebook.com, wikipedia, statista) are present in the accepted pool but should be deprioritized or excluded during evidence extraction. The JMIR and PMC articles are peer-reviewed but cover prior seasons, not the specific task window.
disease_location_time_fit_assessment: Excellent fit for the primary source (CDC FluView 2024-week-40.html: explicitly "Week 40, ending October 5, 2024," United States, influenza). Good fit for MSDH PDF (explicitly "Sept. 29–Oct. 5, 2024," Mississippi, influenza/ILI). Good fit for PAHO bulletin (Epidemiological Week 40, 11 October 2024 publication, Americas/North America, influenza). These marginal sources should be excluded during evidence extraction.
corroboration_potential_assessment: Strong corroboration potential exists between CDC FluView (primary) and PAHO Week 40 bulletin (independent international source citing U.S. data). The ECDC CDTR for the exact date range (Sep 28–Oct 4, 2024) provides a third independent corroborating source. The Mississippi MSDH report corroborates the national low-activity picture at the state level.
